name: Hand Fighting to Remove Collar Grip
summary: Hand fighting in Invisible Collar concerns high-leg and arm connections; stripping a jacket-collar grip requires a separately established cloth choke.
description: Hand fighting in Invisible Collar concerns high-leg and arm connections; stripping a jacket-collar grip requires a separately established cloth choke.

outcomes.to: Cross Collar Choke from Invisible Collar

overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Invisible Collar, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. The word collar does not establish a gi grip. The bottom player owns the leg clinch, and a collar strip is conditional on an opponent actually taking the jacket.

The bottom player faces the kneeling or leaning top player in a high guard. One arm has been isolated through the New York and neck-clearing sequence. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 134 Invisible Collar in Austin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCyIwacRKu8); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): What connection defines the named collar here?
flashcards.answer: Invisible Collar is a facing rubber-guard clinch reinforced by a second high leg; its name does not establish a cloth grip.
flashcards.answer_line: High legs and an arm connection around the upper body

plausible: A hand inserted deep into a jacket lapel
One high shin with the other leg below the waist
trap: A high leg triangle with both opposing arms enclosed

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): What must precede opening a loaded high clinch?
flashcards.answer: Unload the neck and arm before changing the high-leg geometry so the reset does not drag a fixed joint.
flashcards.answer_line: Release the neck and isolated-arm pressure

plausible: Only release the fingers holding your own leg
Only lower the free foot while keeping neck tension
trap: Open the leg crossing while retaining the loaded overhook

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): How should the high leg leave the shoulder line?
flashcards.answer: Use the hips to create space for the leg to lower instead of pulling the foot across a fixed knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Lower it with a comfortable change of hip angle

plausible: Keep the hip still and pull the foot outward
Push the knee down while the ankle stays caught
trap: Flatten your hips before releasing the high ankle grip

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): After hand clearance, what still needs recovery?
flashcards.answer: A freed hand does not prevent chest pressure. Recover inside forearms and knees as the high clinch opens.
flashcards.answer_line: The knee-and-forearm barrier between the bodies

plausible: Only another reach behind their head
Only a forearm frame with both knees still outside
trap: Only the near knee while both hands chase the wrist

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): How do you protect facing posture during the reset?
flashcards.answer: An inside shoulder frame helps prevent a crossface turning your head away while the hips create knee room.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep an inside forearm against the approaching shoulder

plausible: Reach outside their shoulder with the elbow flared
Turn your face away and leave the neck exposed
trap: Keep the forearm low while their shoulder crosses your chest

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): What makes a renewed high-leg attack supportable?
flashcards.answer: Rebuild posture control and knee space before raising the leg again; hand access alone does not restore the clinch.
flashcards.answer_line: Controlled posture with a comfortable supported knee

plausible: Their collar fabric being within reach
Your ankle reaching high while the knee stays pinned
trap: A supported knee with the opponent's chest fully upright

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): What should you recover before raising the high leg again?
flashcards.answer: A new high-leg entry needs the opponent close and your knee supported through available hip space. Freeing a hand or retaining the position name does not re-establish those controls.
flashcards.answer_line: Posture control with comfortable inside knee space

plausible: Only a distant wrist grip with the hips pinned
An unsupported ankle reach around an upright head
trap: Inside knee space with the opponent still leaning away

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): When would a cloth-grip strip actually be relevant?
flashcards.answer: A jacket-grip defense needs an actual cloth connection; the high-leg Invisible Collar name alone is insufficient.
flashcards.answer_line: When the opponent has taken a real jacket grip

plausible: Whenever the second leg goes behind their head
Whenever their hand is outside on the mat
trap: When their hand presses your collarbone through the jacket

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): What supports the hip escape after releasing the grip?
flashcards.answer: Once the high connection or separately present cloth grip has released, keep a forearm inside while the hips admit a knee.
flashcards.answer_line: An inside shoulder frame holding chest pressure away

plausible: Both hands reaching after the opponent's wrist
An outside upper-arm frame with the elbow flared
trap: An inside hand with the forearm folded onto your chest

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): What should a no-gi connection drill identify?
flashcards.answer: In no-gi Invisible Collar, identify the real high-leg and arm connections rather than rehearsing an absent jacket strip.
flashcards.answer_line: The leg-and-arm enclosure, without a fabric grip

plausible: A one-leg posture grip with the second foot at the hip
A high triangle enclosing both opposing elbows
trap: A head clasp with both legs crossed below the shoulders

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (bottom): What is still needed before any rear-control follow-up?
flashcards.answer: Releasing the facing high clinch does not put you behind the opponent; a back-control follow-up needs its own rear attachment.

plausible: Only the opponent's hand leaving your chest
Only the high leg opening around the head
trap: An overhook while still facing the opponent's chest

defender.description: Hand Fighting to Remove Collar Grip (defender): The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip. Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure.
defender.overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Invisible Collar, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. The word collar does not establish a gi grip. The bottom player owns the leg clinch, and a collar strip is conditional on an opponent actually taking the jacket.

The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip. Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure. Avoid driving all weight onto the partner's shoulders while the legs are locked high.

Create space at the hip and thigh before trying to raise the head or extract the arm. Bring the elbow back between the bodies after the high closure opens. Tap immediately to a choke or joint pressure; posture recovery is an early defense, not a late escape guarantee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

The real high-leg enclosure can itself produce vascular choke pressure even when no cloth is held. Protect the neck with early inside hand position, tap if it closes, and let the partner open the leg-and-arm connection before extracting the head.
key_principles: Recognize the high closure: The free leg moving behind your head is an attempt to reinforce posture control, even without a collar grip.
Protect the neck and arm: Keep the head aligned and the captured elbow compact rather than twisting against the enclosure.
Keep a balanced base: Avoid driving all weight onto the partner's shoulders while the legs are locked high.
Address the leg enclosure: Create space at the hip and thigh before trying to raise the head or extract the arm.
Recover inside position: Bring the elbow back between the bodies after the high closure opens.
Stop on compression: Tap immediately to a choke or joint pressure; posture recovery is an early defense, not a late escape guarantee.

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (top): What can hold your head down without a jacket grip?
flashcards.answer: The second high leg reinforces upper-body posture control even when no fabric is held.

plausible: A low ankle crossing behind your waist alone
A hand posted flat on the mat alone
trap: Their arm wrap with both high legs lowered

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (top): How should head and shoulder move while still enclosed?
flashcards.answer: Avoid turning the head or torso away from a captured shoulder; maintain alignment while creating early slack.
flashcards.answer_line: Stay aligned with the captured elbow compact

plausible: Head turned away with the shoulder fixed
Elbow flared while the chest twists inward
trap: Head aligned but the captured elbow extended away

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (top): What does opening the grip need to achieve?
flashcards.answer: The relevant release opens the enclosure around the upper body; simply finding no fabric does not free the head.
flashcards.answer_line: Slack in the high leg-and-arm connection

plausible: An empty hand while the legs remain tight
A wider base with the neck still enclosed
trap: A loose free ankle with the controlling thigh still clamped

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (top): Which early space matters for head recovery?
flashcards.answer: Create slack at the high-leg connection before lifting the head, while keeping the shoulder and neck aligned.
flashcards.answer_line: Space at the hip and thigh of the high leg

plausible: Space between the opponent's fingers only
Space behind your hips while the loop stays tight
trap: Space below the free leg while the high thigh stays close

flashcards.question: Invisible Collar hand fight (top): When the loop opens, where should the elbow go?
flashcards.answer: Recover an inside elbow as the high closure opens so the arm cannot remain isolated outside the guard player's frame.

plausible: Back to a wide mat post outside their hip
Behind the opponent's neck with the elbow flared
trap: Hand on their chest with the elbow outside their knee
